title: Mizzen trust report
description: `trust.json` in the output folder: a build identifier, the review threshold and explicit review instant, plus one entry per rendered content page, keyed by the page URL including `base`. Keys are sorted by code point. Every entry names its stable `key`, its `url`, its `source`, the state of each evidence signal, `level`, the ordered `factors` behind it, the `provenance` of each signal, `reviewCoverage`, `reasons`, and, when known, `lastReviewer`, in that order. `build.id` is a deterministic hash of the final HTML documents the build renders, layouts included, so evidence can be joined to the build that produced them. `asOf` is present only when the caller named the review instant, never when the wall clock would have supplied one. Two builds with the same model, data, root, and `SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH` write the same bytes. App and asset pages are left out.

build.description: The identity of the rendered pages the evidence belongs to.

id.description: SHA-256 over every doc page's key, Markdown hash, and final HTML hash, sorted by URL. The HTML is the document the build writes, layout included, so changing a page's URL, source, Markdown, or layout-rendered HTML changes it.

pages.description: How many rendered content pages the build has.

reviewDueDays.description: The review-due threshold, in whole days, that the levels were judged with.

asOf.description: The explicit instant review ages were measured from. Absent when the caller named none; the wall clock is never substituted.

pages.description: One entry per rendered content page, keyed by the page URL including `base`, in code-point order.

key.description: Stable page key: SHA-256 of the page's URL, a NUL, and its source file. The same page has the same key across builds.

source.description: The source file, relative to the site root, with forward slashes.

evidence.description: What each signal measured, or why it did not. `missing` means no source for the signal existed; `unknown` means a source existed but gave no answer. A signal that is not `measured` also has an explaining reason.

examples.description: `measured`, `none` when the page declares no test fence, or `unknown` when it declares examples but their result is unavailable.

drift.description: `measured`, `missing` when no drift data or root was available, or `unknown` when a source existed but gave no usable answer (a malformed data entry, or a check that named no count).

review.description: `measured`, `missing` when no reviewer data or root was available, or `unknown` when a data entry or git named no readable date.

level.description: The worst level the reasons support: `at-risk` beats `review-due` beats `verified`.

factors.description: Exactly three signals as data, in the fixed order examples, drift, review, with the same code as the matching reason.

provenance.description: Where each signal's answer came from, whether that source could answer, and the input it read.

reviewCoverage.description: What the review source knows: `recorded` when it names a review, `untracked` when a work tree has no commit for the file, `unavailable` when git or the path inside the root is missing, `unknown` when no source was asked.

reasons.description: Exactly three reasons, in the fixed order examples, drift, review.

lastReviewer.description: The author name of the last commit that touched the page's source, when git or the data file names one; absent otherwise.

code.description: The same stable identifier as the matching reason.

state.description: Whether the evidence is good, neutral, absent, bad, or contradictory.

value.description: The measured value: failing examples for examples, findings for drift, and whole days for review; `unknown` when it was not measured. A negative day count means the review is dated after the measured instant, which is a conflict.

source.description: `inline` for the caller's or site's data, or `none` when no data and no test fence exist.

input.description: The page URL for inline data.

source.description: `inline` for supplied data, `computed` for the drift pass over the site root, or `none` when neither was available.

input.description: The page URL for inline data, or the source file for a computed pass.

source.description: `inline` for supplied data, `git` for the source file's history, or `none` when neither was available.

input.description: The page URL for inline data, or the source file for git.

availability.description: `available` when the source answered, `unavailable` when it existed but could not answer, `missing` when no source existed, `not-applicable` when the page has no such signal, or `conflict` when the answer contradicts other evidence.

code.description: A stable identifier for one finding. `examples.unknown` is the output's own code: the page declares examples but their result is unavailable, so the page cannot be verified.

message.description: The sentence a maintainer reads to see what the code found.
